text: @dotey 佬 一般工作5.5 思考强度开的多少呀？

大家好，Magpie 今天有一个很重要的更新，就是 Magpie 中的 Claude Code Provider 的实现方式，从之前的使用 claude -p 改为了直接使用 Claude Code TUI。当然这是可配置的，你可以设置回以前的方案。

关于为何做这个改动，其实一开始我是不太情愿的，因为使用 Claude Code TUI 去做这个实现的话，会特别多额外的工作。收益不是很高，甚至 streaming 没法完美实现。但是最近发生了一件事情，让我觉得我不得不得不做这个改动了，就是有人发现直接使用 claude -p 在 5 小时窗口情况下，会比用 Claude Code TUI 多花两倍的 Token（虽然 Claude 今天已经取消了5小时窗口，但是我不确定 Anthropic 以后会不会有其他的区别对待）

换成直接用 TUI 方式实现，除了能够让我们的额度消耗跟直接使用 TUI 一模一样之外，另外一个更大的优势就是在 Magpie 使用 Claude Code Provider 跟用户直接使用 Claude Code TUI 是一模一样的，几乎没有了被检测出来在第三方使用导致封号的风险。

https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/97074#issuecomment-6426128541

quoted_tweet.author: lauren
quoted_tweet.text:
here’s a short grok bot guide on how i create high quality bots and manage my team. ask @bot to read this post and help you improve your team!

• add dr eggbot to your team! he’s my bot designer that i use to create bots
• you don’t need a lot of bots. a few good bots can be more useful and easier to manage than a large team
• tell your bots to create skills for itself as you give it instructions on how to do tasks. this lets them do them more consistently even over long conversations. you can even ask it to create a private github repo for you to store all your skills if you want them preserved independently
• add connectors, use the vault, and give access to all the tools you use to do your work. you can also ask your bot to setup its own email and it can sign up for its own accounts for better separation 
• thinking about all the work you do by hand, or steps in your workflows where you have to copy and paste information back to your bot. ask your bot how it can do that for you instead!
• imagine you hired an intern, how would you onboard them and help them do the work correctly and efficiently? introduce yourself to your bot and describe the work you do, then ask it how it can help you automate it

and my favorite tip: use voice mode or the transcription option! it’s a good way to just brain dump a lot of information. then, at the end, tell your bot to “restate this in your own words” so you can confirm it understood you

https://x.ai/bot/_jOdbfkB16zxu7MRcmReE

The thing with AI transformation is that one agent can deliver 25M worth of value to a business per year

While another agent delivers just 0.25M

And they’re the exact same effort to make

AI transformation for an org of 5000 isn’t that much more difficult than an org of 500, but the returns are over 10x larger because inefficiencies scale exponentially with headcount 

This is why enterprise adopts faster, not slower, than mid-market

a16z's Moses Sternstein on the AI jobs panic, what job postings actually show, and why technical hiring is running hot:

"People are saying, 'Oh, AI's already killing jobs.'... but right now it's almost certainly not."

"Even human resources, right? Which is considered the front line of future demand hiring... That has basically returned to baseline. And software development, that's been a pretty good run."

"Engineering, software development, manufacturing... this is job openings, it's Indeed, it's one data set, but they're on a tear. I think it's even fair to call it hot."

"I think that's partly why at least the top line FUD discourse has faded. It'd be nice if they kind of inverted and be like, actually it turns out that there's been a pretty incredible job run as a result of AI, or at least coterminous with AI."

@MosesSternstein @alex_danco

a16z's Moses Sternstein and Alex Danco on the "rack spread," the gap between rising GPU prices and falling token prices:

"The core observation in the rack spread is as follows: roughly since the summer, GPU pricing has gone up, token pricing has gone down. Why that is: a combination of open competition, the labs themselves cutting prices."

"We start with a bunch of GPUs and a bunch of electricity and a bunch of cooling, and on the other side out comes tokens, right? And the thing that achieves that is the model."

"In an oil refinery, you have a bunch of inputs... It goes into a refinery, which is like the model, and then out come refined products that you can actually use, like jet fuel or diesel or lubricant or any number of specialized things."

"There is this term called the crack spread... It's not a net margin that anybody is actually making... But it is useful because if you look at any given refinery, just like you might look at any given model, you want to ask this basic question which is, 'Is this making any money?'"

@MosesSternstein @alex_danco
